1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# prepare_env.sh — sourced by platform after base image startup
3	# Do NOT set -euo pipefail here (sourced script should not exit the parent shell)
4	
5	echo "[prepare_env] start $(date '+%F %T')"
6	
7	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
8	
9	# 1. Install our custom SGLang (replaces image built-in version)
10	uv pip install --no-deps -e "${SCRIPT_DIR}/sglang/python"
11	
12	# 2. Install nvidia-modelopt (inference) + llmcompressor (GPTQ quantization)
13	uv pip install "nvidia-modelopt==0.42.0" "llmcompressor==[REDACTED]"
14	
15	# 2.1 Upgrade cuDNN to 9.20+ (fixes FP4 cuDNN backend on SM120)
16	uv pip install "nvidia-cudnn-cu12>=9.15.0"
17	echo "[prepare_env] cuDNN upgraded: $(python3 -c 'import cudnn; print(f"backend={cudnn.backend_version()} frontend={cudnn.__version__}")')"
18	
19	# 2.2 Upgrade FlashInfer (newer CUTLASS FP4 kernels for SM120, fixes NaN/corruption)
20	uv pip install "flashinfer-python>=0.6.7" "flashinfer-cubin>=0.6.7"
21	echo "[prepare_env] FlashInfer upgraded: $(python3 -c 'import flashinfer; print(flashinfer.__version__)')"
22	# Clear entire JIT cache — new version must rebuild all kernels
23	rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer/
24	echo "[prepare_env] cleared FlashInfer JIT cache for clean rebuild"
25	
26	# 3. Patch llmcompressor: FourOverSix adaptive scale=4/6 selection (arXiv:2512.02010)
27	GPTQ_TARGET=[REDACTED]
28	cp "${SCRIPT_DIR}/patches/gptq_quantize_fouroversix.py" "$GPTQ_TARGET"
29	echo "[prepare_env] patched gptq_quantize.py with FourOverSix"
30	
31	# 4. Replace sgl-kernel .so with pre-built version (Marlin FP4 scale fix)
32	INSTALLED_SO="/opt/SGLang-MiniCPM-SALA/sglang_minicpm_sala_env/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sgl_kernel/sm100/common_ops.abi3.so"
33	cp "$INSTALLED_SO" "${INSTALLED_SO}.bak"
34	cp "${SCRIPT_DIR}/common_ops.abi3.so" "$INSTALLED_SO"
35	echo "[prepare_env] replaced common_ops.abi3.so ($(stat -c%s "${SCRIPT_DIR}/common_ops.abi3.so") bytes)"
36	
37	# 5. Fix FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 GEMM PDL race on SM120.
38	#    The stock FlashInfer 0.5.3 JIT recipe for fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120 misses
39	#    the GDC flag, which can produce NaNs on long-context chunked prefill in a
40	#    cold environment. Patch the JIT recipe before server startup and clear the
41	#    cached op so the kernel is rebuilt with the correct flag.
42	FLASHINFER_GEMM_CORE=[REDACTED]
43	if grep -q 'fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120' "$FLASHINFER_GEMM_CORE" && ! grep -q 'CUTLASS_ENABLE_GDC_FOR_SM100' "$FLASHINFER_GEMM_CORE"; then
44	    sed -i '/"fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120"/,/extra_cflags/{
45	        s/"-DENABLE_FP4",/"-DENABLE_FP4",\n            "-DCUTLASS_ENABLE_GDC_FOR_SM100=1",/
46	    }' "$FLASHINFER_GEMM_CORE"
47	    rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer/*/120a/cached_ops/fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120/
48	    echo "[prepare_env] patched FlashInfer SM120 FP4 GEMM with GDC flag, cleared JIT cache"
49	fi
50	
51	# 5.1 Pre-build the FlashInfer SM120 FP4 GEMM JIT op so the eval server does
52	#     not have to compile it on first use. This makes the cold-start platform
53	#     state closer to the local hot-cache state.
54	python3 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/prewarm_flashinfer_fp4.py"
55	
56	# 6. Set inference parameters
57	#    Override SGLANG_SERVER_ARGS entirely (platform default has --attention-backend flashinfer,
58	#    we need minicpm_flashinfer; also add EAGLE-3 speculative decoding flags).
59	SPEC_STEPS="${EAGLE_SPEC_STEPS:-3}"
60	TOPK="${EAGLE_TOPK:-1}"
61	DTN=$((1 + TOPK * SPEC_STEPS))
62	EAGLE_DRAFT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/data/eagle_draft"
63	export SGLANG_SERVER_ARGS="--disable-radix-cache --attention-backend minicpm_flashinfer --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --skip-server-warmup --dense-as-sparse --quantization modelopt_fp4 --max-running-requests 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 --speculative-num-steps ${SPEC_STEPS} --speculative-eagle-topk ${TOPK} --speculative-num-draft-tokens ${DTN} --speculative-draft-attention-backend flashinfer --speculative-draft-model-path ${EAGLE_DRAFT}"
64	export SGLANG_MARLIN_DECODE_THRESHOLD=48
65	export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=":4096:8"
66	
67	echo "[prepare_env] EAGLE defaults: steps=${SPEC_STEPS} topk=${TOPK} dtn=${DTN} draft=${EAGLE_DRAFT}"
68	echo "[prepare_env] SGLANG_SERVER_ARGS=${SGLANG_SERVER_ARGS}"
69	echo "[prepare_env] SGLANG_MARLIN_DECODE_THRESHOLD=${SGLANG_MARLIN_DECODE_THRESHOLD}"
70	
71	# 7. Email notification — env ready
72	env_body="/tmp/demo_sala_env_ready.txt"
73	{
74	    echo "prepare_env completed on $(date '+%F %T')"
75	    echo
76	    echo "SGLANG_SERVER_ARGS=${SGLANG_SERVER_ARGS}"
77	    echo "SGLANG_MARLIN_DECODE_THRESHOLD=${SGLANG_MARLIN_DECODE_THRESHOLD}"
78	    echo "CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=${CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG}"
79	    echo
80	    echo "===== pip freeze (key packages) ====="
81	    python3 -c "import sglang, torch, flashinfer, cudnn, llmcompressor; print(f'sglang={sglang.__version__} torch={torch.__version__} flashinfer={flashinfer.__version__} cudnn_frontend={cudnn.__version__} cudnn_backend={cudnn.backend_version()} llmcompressor={llmcompressor.__version__}')" 2>&1 || true
82	    echo
83	    echo "===== nvidia-smi ====="
84	    nvidia-smi || true
85	} > "$env_body"
86	python3 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/probe_email.py" \
87	    --subject "[demo-sala] 1/3 env ready" \
88	    --body-file "$env_body" || echo "[prepare_env] env email FAILED"
89	
90	echo "[prepare_env] done $(date '+%F %T')"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -eo pipefail
3	# prepare_model.sh — called by platform as:
4	#   bash prepare_model.sh --input <original_model_path> --output <output_model_path>
5	
6	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
7	QUANT_LOG="${SCRIPT_DIR}/quant_log.txt"
8	
9	echo "[prepare_model] start $(date '+%F %T')"
10	echo "[prepare_model] args: $*"
11	
12	# Email 2/3 — GPU memory snapshot before preprocess
13	gpu_body="/tmp/demo_sala_gpu_mem.txt"
14	{
15	    echo "prepare_model starting on $(date '+%F %T')"
16	    echo "args: $*"
17	    echo
18	    echo "===== nvidia-smi ====="
19	    nvidia-smi || true
20	    echo
21	    echo "===== torch.cuda.mem_get_info ====="
22	    python3 -c "import torch; free,total=torch.cuda.mem_get_info(); print(f'free={free/1024**3:.2f} GB  total={total/1024**3:.2f} GB  used={(total-free)/1024**3:.2f} GB')" 2>&1 || true
23	    echo
24	    echo "===== GPU processes (fuser) ====="
25	    fuser -v /dev/nvidia* 2>&1 || true
26	} > "$gpu_body"
27	python3 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/probe_email.py" \
28	    --subject "[demo-sala] 2/3 gpu mem before quant" \
29	    --body-file "$gpu_body" || echo "[prepare_model] gpu-mem email FAILED"
30	
31	# GPTQ + NVFP4 + FourOverSix quantization
32	export PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
33	export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
34	export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=":4096:8"
35	echo "[prepare_model] starting quantization (GPTQ+FourOverSix, 90K, calib90, deterministic)"
36	set +e
37	python3 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/preprocess_model.py" "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$QUANT_LOG"
38	quant_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
39	set -e
40	echo "[prepare_model] preprocess exit_code=${quant_rc}"
41	
42	# Email 3/3 — quant done (or failed)
43	quant_body="/tmp/demo_sala_quant_done.txt"
44	{
45	    echo "Quantization finished on $(date '+%F %T')"
46	    echo "exit_code=${quant_rc}"
47	    echo "args: $*"
48	    echo
49	    echo "===== nvidia-smi ====="
50	    nvidia-smi || true
51	    echo
52	    echo "===== quant_log tail (400) ====="
53	    tail -n 400 "$QUANT_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
54	} > "$quant_body"
55	subj_status=$([ "$quant_rc" = "0" ] && echo "done" || echo "FAILED")
56	python3 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/probe_email.py" \
57	    --subject "[demo-sala] 3/3 quant ${subj_status}" \
58	    --body-file "$quant_body" \
59	    --attach "$QUANT_LOG" || echo "[prepare_model] quant email FAILED"
60	
61	echo "[prepare_model] done $(date '+%F %T')"
62	exit "$quant_rc"
63

> DEVELOPER

背景：推理优化项目评估 CUDA 12.8 → CUDA 13 升级。硬件 RTX 6000D (sm_120 Blackwell)，重度依赖 NVFP4 GEMM、Marlin FP4 W4A16、Triton 自写 kernel。今天日期 2026-04-20。

用 WebFetch/WebSearch 调研以下，给出具体版本和链接：
1. **CUTLASS**：4.x 最新版对 Blackwell NVFP4 GEMM 的改进（CuTe DSL、WGMMA、TMA 新模板），以及 cu13 的支持状态
2. **sgl-kernel**（SGLang 的 kernel 包）：0.3.x 及之后版本对 cu13 / Blackwell 的支持，Marlin FP4 相关修复进度（GitHub: sgl-project/sglang）
3. **Triton**：当前版本（3.x 之后？）对 sm_120 的原生支持，nvcc 13 + CUDA 13 runtime 下 Triton kernel 是否有新优化路径
4. **DeepGemm**：对 Blackwell FP4/FP8 的支持进展（DeepSeek 出的）
5. **nvcc 13 vs 12.8**：对 Triton 生成的 PTX 在 sm_120 下 lowering 质量是否有实测对比

格式：每项 (最新版本, cu13 状态, 对 Blackwell 的关键收益, 源 URL)。<400 字。事实优先。

## Current Status

The latest PyTorch stable releases support only up to sm_90, meaning official support for sm_120 (Blackwell architecture) has not yet been included in stable releases as of the current date.

## Nightly Build Support

PyTorch nightly builds (e.g., 2.10.0.dev + cu12.9) can detect sm_120, but they are not yet fully stable. However, the search results indicate that PyTorch Nightly with cu128 or cu129 provides proper sm_120 support.

## CUDA Version Notes

It's worth noting that CUDA 12.8/12.9 already includes support for Blackwell architectures. The search results discuss CUDA 12.x versions more prominently than CUDA 13 specifically.

## User Workarounds

Since official stable wheels with sm_120 support are not yet available, some workarounds exist such as building from source with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="sm_120".

The search results don't contain specific information about a PyTorch 2.10 release with official CUDA 13 wheels for Blackwell sm_120, suggesting that this combination may not yet be available in stable releases.

Based on the web search results, here are the key findings regarding cuDNN 9.16, 9.17, and attention heuristic improvements for Blackwell:

## cuDNN 9.16.0 Release Notes

Scaled dot-product attention bprop performance has been significantly improved on Blackwell-architecture GPUs (compute capability 10.0), with benchmarking showing performance improvements of between 7% and 25%.

## cuDNN 9.15.0 Release Notes

Performance has been further optimized for 16-bit data type input, with these optimizations inspired by flash attention v4 for Blackwell-architecture GPUs. Users can disable these optimizations by setting the environment variables CUDNN_RESCALE_THRESHOLD and CUDNN_USE_EX2_EMULATION to 0, with defaults using CUDNN_RESCALE_THRESHOLD=8 and CUDNN_USE_EX2_EMULATION=1.

## cuDNN 9.17.0 Updates

The benchmark results for the SDPA improvements added in cuDNN 9.17.0 were updated in the cudnn-frontend releases.

## Bug Fixes and Known Issues

An issue that caused scaled dot-product attention statistics to be incorrect if the statistics are not in BHSD layout on Blackwell GPU architectures has been fixed, with statistics now allowed to be any layout.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding CUDA 13, Blackwell support, and FP4 improvements:

## CUDA 13 and Blackwell Support

CUDA 13.0 supports all NVIDIA architectures from Turing through Grace Blackwell. More specifically, CUDA 13.0 features support for sm_110 (Jetson Thor), sm_103 (B300/GB300), and sm_121 (DGX SPARK/DIGITS), with CUDA 12.9 first introducing sm_12x architecture support compatible with sm_120.

## FP4 Improvements

The experimental Grouped GEMM API in cuBLASLt was extended to support NVFP4 inputs and bias epilogues on Blackwell GPUs with Compute Capability 10.x and 11.0 in CUDA 13.2 Update 1. Grouped GEMM performance on Blackwell GPUs was improved, providing up to 20% higher performance for large problem sizes.

Additionally, CUDA Toolkit 12.9 introduced block-scaled FP4 and FP8 matmuls on NVIDIA Blackwell, and CUDA 13.1 added performance support for these data types and BF16.

## NVCC Improvements

NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer 2025.4 added support for NVIDIA CUDA Compiler (NVCC) compile-time patching through the -fdevice-sanitize=memcheck compiler flag, which enhances memory error detection and improves compute sanitizer performance through compile-time instrumentation that integrates error detection directly into NVCC.

1	"""Optimized SimpleGLA decode kernel with BK=BV=128.
2	
3	FLA's default kernel uses BK=BV=min(next_power_of_2(K), 64), producing
4	4x more blocks than needed for K=V=128 (Grid=128 vs 32 per head-batch).
5	This kernel uses BK=BV=128 to match MiniCPM-SALA's head_dim exactly,
6	giving ~2.4x speedup at low batch sizes.
7	
8	Only supports the SimpleGLA decode path: T=1 (or small T), g_gamma decay,
9	no g/gk/gv gates, no reverse. Falls back to FLA for unsupported configs.
10	"""
11	
12	import torch
13	import triton
14	import triton.language as tl
15	
16	from fla.ops.utils.op import exp
17	
18	
19	@triton.heuristics({
20	    'USE_INITIAL_STATE': lambda args: args['h0'] is not None,
21	    'STORE_FINAL_STATE': lambda args: args['ht'] is not None,
22	    'IS_VARLEN': lambda args: args['cu_seqlens'] is not None,
23	})
24	@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=['B', 'T'])
25	def _simple_gla_decode_kernel(
26	    q, k, v, g_gamma, o, h0, ht, cu_seqlens, scale,
27	    B, T,
28	    H: tl.constexpr,
29	    K: tl.constexpr,
30	    V: tl.constexpr,
31	    BK: tl.constexpr,
32	    BV: tl.constexpr,
33	    USE_INITIAL_STATE: tl.constexpr,
34	    STORE_FINAL_STATE: tl.constexpr,
35	    IS_VARLEN: tl.constexpr,
36	):
37	    i_v, i_k, i_nh = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64), tl.program_id(1).to(tl.int64), tl.program_id(2).to(tl.int64)
38	    i_n, i_h = i_nh // H, i_nh % H
39	
40	    all = B * T
41	    if IS_VARLEN:
42	        bos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n).to(tl.int64)
43	        eos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n + 1).to(tl.int64)
44	        T = eos - bos
45	    else:
46	        bos = i_n * T
47	
48	    o_k = i_k * BK + tl.arange(0, BK)
49	    o_v = i_v * BV + tl.arange(0, BV)
50	    m_k = o_k < K
51	    m_v = o_v < V
52	    m_h = m_k[:, None] & m_v[None, :]
53	
54	    b_h = tl.zeros([BK, BV], dtype=tl.float32)
55	    if USE_INITIAL_STATE:
56	        p_h0 = h0 + i_nh * K * V + o_k[:, None] * V + o_v[None, :]
57	        b_h += tl.load(p_h0, mask=m_h, other=0).to(tl.float32)
58	
59	    b_g_gamma = tl.load(g_gamma + i_h)
60	
61	    p_q = q + bos * H * K + i_h * K + o_k
62	    p_k = k + bos * H * K + i_h * K + o_k
63	    p_v = v + bos * H * V + i_h * V + o_v
64	    p_o = o + (i_k * all + bos) * H * V + i_h * V + o_v
65	
66	    for _ in range(0, T):
67	        b_q = tl.load(p_q, mask=m_k, other=0).to(tl.float32) * scale
68	        b_k = tl.load(p_k, mask=m_k, other=0).to(tl.float32)
69	        b_v = tl.load(p_v, mask=m_v, other=0).to(tl.float32)
70	        b_h = b_h * exp(b_g_gamma)
71	        b_h += b_k[:, None] * b_v[None, :]
72	        b_o = b_h * b_q[:, None]
73	        b_o = tl.sum(b_o, axis=0)
74	        tl.store(p_o, b_o.to(p_o.dtype.element_ty), mask=m_v)
75	        p_q += H * K
76	        p_k += H * K
77	        p_v += H * V
78	        p_o += H * V
79

## Key Features & Support

CUTLASS has been providing support for block scaled data types including NVIDIA NVFP4 across NVIDIA's Volta, Turing, Ampere, Ada, Hopper, and Blackwell architectures.

CUTLASS 4 adds CUTLASS DSLs, which are Python native interfaces for writing high-performance CUDA kernels based on core CUTLASS and CuTe concepts without any performance compromises.

## CUDA Support

The latest releases have optimal code generation with CUDA toolkit versions 13.2. Recent releases mention optimal code generation with CUDA toolkit versions 13.1.

## CuTe Integration

CUTLASS 3.0 and beyond adopts CuTe throughout the GEMM hierarchy in its templates. CuTe DSL is currently in public beta and will graduate out of beta by end of summer 2025.

## Blackwell NVFP4 GEMM Support

Recent releases include multiple examples and fixes for Blackwell NVFP4 support:
- Fixes for core dump issues for nvfp4 grouped GEMM kernel
- Examples demonstrating Blockscaled GEMM with NVFP4 input datatype and BF16 output tensor, and NVFP4 output tensor with scale factor generation

CUTLASS 4.x builds are known to be down on Windows platforms for all CUDA toolkits.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding sgl-kernel 0.3, CUDA 13, Blackwell SM_120, Marlin, and FP4 support in 2026:

## Key Findings

**Blackwell SM_120 FP4 Support Status:**
SM120 (RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell, compute capability 12.0) is not recognized in the MXFP4 backend selection logic, causing fallback to Marlin instead of using native NVFP4 kernels.

**SGLang/sgl-kernel Compatibility Issues:**
There have been compatibility issues with SGLang/sgl-kernel with Blackwell GPUs (SM_120) on CUDA 12.8, with solutions involving manual installation of sgl-kernel wheel files from the GitHub whl repository.

**Recent Progress on Blackwell Support:**
SGLang released sglang-kernel 0.4.1 with renamed package (sgl-kernel → sglang-kernel), consolidated kernels, and cleanup of deprecated ops, and SGLang achieved a 145 TFLOPS gap advantage over vLLM on FP4 MoE inference through systematic kernel engineering including kernel fusion and Blackwell-specific CUTLASS schedules.

**Marlin Kernel Issues:**
Users report warnings that their GPU does not have native FP4 support and weight-only FP4 compression falls back to leveraging the Marlin kernel.

The search results indicate active development in 2025-2026 to improve FP4 support on Blackwell SM_120, though some compatibility and performance issues remain.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Triton 3.x, sm_120 Blackwell support, CUDA, and nvcc:

## Triton 3.x and Blackwell Support

Triton 3.3 and later officially supports Blackwell with CUDA 12.8 or higher and PyTorch 2.7 or later.

## sm_120 and Blackwell Architecture

CUDA Toolkit 12.8 added Blackwell architecture options including sm_120, which represents compute capability 12.0 for Blackwell GPUs like the RTX 5090 and RTX 50-series GPUs.

## CUDA Support for Blackwell

With CUDA Toolkit 12.8, nvcc can generate cubin native to the Blackwell architecture (compute capability 10.0). Additionally, CUDA 13.0 supports all NVIDIA architectures from Turing through Blackwell, featuring sm_110 (Jetson Thor), sm_103 (B300/GB300), and sm_121 (DGX SPARK/DIGITS).

## CUDA 13 and Recent Developments

The search results indicate that CUDA 13.x is being used in current development environments. CUDA 13.x CCCL headers require a standard conforming preprocessor, and recent configurations include VS 2026, CUDA 13.2, PyTorch 2.11.0, and RTX 5090 (Blackwell, sm_120).

## DeepGEMM 2026.04.16 Release

On April 16, 2026, DeepGEMM released a major update featuring Mega MoE, FP8xFP4 GEMM, FP4 Indexer, PDL, and faster JIT compilation.

### Key Features:

**Mega MoE**: Mega MoE fuses and overlaps EP dispatch, linear 1 (FP8xFP4), SwiGLU, linear 2 (FP8xFP4), and EP combine into a single mega-kernel, overlapping NVLink communication and tensor core computation. Currently, it only supports FP8 x FP4 MoE, EP≤8, and requires PyTorch≥2.9.

**FP4 Support**: The update also adds FP4 Indexer (for MQA logits, supporting larger MTP), FP8 x FP4 GEMM, PDL, and DeepEPv2 MoE GEMM layout.

### Blackwell (SM100) Architecture Support:

DeepGEMM is optimized for deep learning workloads on NVIDIA Hopper (SM90) and Blackwell (SM100) GPU architectures. As of July 20, 2025, DeepGEMM now supports both SM90/SM100 with a full refactor including a low-CPU-overhead JIT CPP module.

### Related Blackwell/NVFP4 Developments:

For DeepSeek-V3.2, NVIDIA's NVFP4 quantization reduced the memory footprint of the model by 1.7x compared to the model's original FP8 format (415 GB vs. 690 GB), demonstrating practical benefits of FP4 support on Blackwell hardware.

## PyTorch 2.10 with CUDA 13.0 (cu130)

PyTorch 2.10.0 is available for CUDA 13.0 with the installation command: `pip install torch==2.10.0 torchvision==0.25.0 torchaudio==2.10.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130`

This command installs from the official PyTorch wheel repository. The wheels are hosted at `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130`, which is the standard index for CUDA 13.0 builds.

If you need to download the wheels manually instead of using pip, you can access them directly from the PyTorch download repository at that URL, where you'll find the `.whl` files for torch, torchvision, and torchaudio matching your Python version and platform.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about CUDA 13 vs CUDA 12.8 with Blackwell SM120 NVFP4 GEMM benchmarks. Here are the key findings:

## CUDA Toolkit Selection for SM120 Blackwell

As of March 2026, the optimal combination for using llama.cpp on Blackwell is CUDA 12.8 + MMQ. When you build with CUDA 13.1, the Blackwell MMQ kernel crashes with a Segmentation fault. NVIDIA's official migration guide also explicitly recommends building llama.cpp for Blackwell (SM120) with CUDA 12.8.

## NVFP4 GEMM Compatibility Issues

There have been significant compatibility issues with NVFP4 GEMM operations on SM120 desktop Blackwell GPUs:

All native FP4 MoE backends produce garbage output or crash on SM120 (compute_120) due to broken CUTLASS grouped GEMM templates. The issues stem from differences between compute_120a and compute_120f architectures.

The f suffix enables the "full" SM120 feature set with working TMA WS grouped GEMM tactics. compute_120f enabled the fast TMA WS grouped GEMM tactics that failed with compute_120a. This confirms the f suffix is the correct architecture designation for SM120 desktop Blackwell GPUs.

## Performance Improvements in CUDA 13.2

cuBLASLt now delivers up to 3× performance improvement for NVFP4 and MXFP8 data types on DGX Spark systems for large M and N problem sizes. However, this specifically applies to DGX Spark (SM121), not the consumer SM120 architecture.

## Summary

While CUDA 13.0+ supports compute_120f with proper NVFP4 GEMM functionality, **CUDA 12.8 is the recommended stable baseline** for Blackwell SM120 systems. CUDA 13.x has shown issues with certain workloads (like llama.cpp's MMQ kernels) and should be used with caution for SM120 specifically.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Blackwell performance improvements with FP4 TFLOPS:

## Blackwell FP4 Performance

Blackwell achieves FP4 throughput of 3850.1 TFLOPS at m64n8k16 configuration, demonstrating strong native support for ultra-low-precision compute.

## Performance Improvements Over Previous Generations

Compared to Hopper, Blackwell achieves 4x improvement in FP4 operations, marking a significant leap in low-precision performance. While the base Blackwell architecture delivers 10 petaFLOPS of NVFP4 performance, Blackwell Ultra pushes that to 15 petaFLOPS—a 1.5x increase compared to standard Blackwell GPU and 7.5x increase from NVIDIA Hopper H100 and H200 GPUs.

## CUDA Support

Blackwell maintains full software compatibility with previous NVIDIA architectures with CUDA 12.x support, providing full backward compatibility with existing CUDA code and new intrinsics for TMEM access.

## NVFP4 Format Advantages

NVIDIA NVFP4, the new 4-bit floating-point format in Blackwell, combines two-level scaling and delivers nearly FP8-equivalent accuracy (with often less than ~1% difference), while reducing memory footprint by ~1.8x compared to FP8 and up to ~3.5x vs. FP16.

The search results confirm that Blackwell's FP4 capabilities represent a major advancement in low-precision AI compute, with significant performance gains over previous generation hardware.

I've found relevant search results about CUTLASS, CUDA 13, NVFP4, and Blackwell SM100/SM120 architectures. Here's what I found:

## Support and Implementation

CUTLASS has been providing CUDA C++ template abstractions for high-performance linear algebra since 2017 with support for NVIDIA NVFP4 and other block-scaled data types across multiple architectures including Blackwell.

CUTLASS has optimal code generation with CUDA toolkit versions 13.2.

## Blackwell Architecture Support

CUTLASS 3.x API supports Blackwell SM120 kernels for GeForce GPUs with full epilogue and EVT fusions, including examples demonstrating blockscaled GEMM with NVFP4 input datatype.

CUTLASS includes grouped GEMM for vanilla FP8 data inputs and NVFP4 block scaled inputs.

## SM100 Performance

CUTLASS 3.8's performance shows high theoretical peak utilization on various input and output data types when run on NVIDIA Blackwell SM100 architecture GPU.

## SM120 Issues and Workarounds

However, there have been significant issues with SM120 (desktop Blackwell): Issues with CUTLASS grouped GEMM templates resulted in reduced speed (14.6 tok/s vs Marlin's 46-49 tok/s) due to autotuner falling back to slow kernel tactics after TMA WS grouped GEMM initialization failures.

Using CUDA 13.0 with the "f" suffix (compute_120f) enables the "full" SM120 feature set with working TMA WS grouped GEMM tactics.

Based on the search results, I found some relevant information about NVCC, PTX, and Triton codegen, though I did not find specific benchmark comparisons between NVCC 13 and 12.8 for Triton PTX sm_120 codegen performance in 2026.

Here's what I found:

**NVCC and sm_120 Support:**
SM_120 (compute_120f) was added in CUDA 12.9 and is compatible with all CC 12.x devices (sm_120, sm_121). The sm_101 architecture was renumbered to sm_110 in CUDA 13.0.

**Triton and PTX Codegen:**
Triton uses LLVM which generates different PTX than NVCC, and Triton optimizes and lowers code to LLVM-IR/MLIR before generating PTX directly through libLLVM. Triton uses the standard LLVM compiler back-end with the NVPTX target to automatically translate its intermediate representation (Triton-IR/MLIR) into optimised PTX assembly code.

**Recent CUDA Compiler Features:**
CUDA added a new compiler option --Ofast-compile=<level> in version 13, which prioritizes faster compilation over optimizations at varying levels.

Unfortunately, the search results don't contain specific performance benchmark data comparing NVCC 13 vs 12.8 for Triton PTX sm_120 codegen in 2026. You may want to consult NVIDIA's official benchmarking reports, Triton's GitHub repository, or academic papers on GPU compiler performance for this specific comparison.

# CUTLASS 4.4.2 Release Summary

**Latest Version:** 4.4.2 (Released March 17, 2025)

**CUDA 13 Support:** Yes - The release notes specifically mention "Enable Blackwell SM120f compilation of examples and exposes NVFP4/MX Grouped GEMM in the CUTLASS Profiler" for CUDA toolkit compatibility.

## Key Changelog Highlights

**CuTe DSL Improvements:**
- Python 3.14 support added for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures
- "Runtime Pointer/Tensor/FakeTensor now supports **cache_key**, providing a stable, hashable representation" for improved kernel caching
- Fixed Hopper FMHA causal attention performance issues on CUDA 13.1 through mbarrier optimization

**Blackwell Architecture (SM_120/SM_121):**
- SM120f compilation enabled with explicit NVFP4 and MX grouped GEMM support in the profiler
- Block-scaled GEMM operations exposed for grouped matrix multiplication workloads

**Infrastructure:**
- Resolved kernel loading race conditions affecting multi-GPU JAX deployments

The 4.4.2 release focuses on stability improvements and expanding hardware support for newer GPU architectures while maintaining backward compatibility.

Based on the GitHub releases page, here are the key details:

## Latest Release
**v0.5.10** (April 6, 2024) is the current stable version, with a hotfix **v0.5.10.post1** released April 9, 2024.

## sglang-kernel Status
The project recently underwent a major kernel package reorganization:
- **sglang-kernel 0.4.1** is the latest version (renamed from sgl-kernel)
- Includes consolidated kernels and deprecated operation cleanup
- Supports **SM120 Blackwell GPUs** with dedicated optimizations
- CUDA 13 wheels are available

## Key v0.5.10 Highlights
Major features include piecewise CUDA graph execution by default, elastic expert parallelism for fault tolerance on MoE models, GPU staging buffers for disaggregated prefill/decode, and sparse attention via HiSparse integration.

## Notable Improvements
- FlashInfer MXFP8 kernel support for mixed-precision inference
- Transformers 5.3.0 upgrade enabling latest HuggingFace models
- LoRA support extended to Mixture-of-Experts layers
- Native MLX backend for Apple Silicon devices
- Multiple new model support (Nemotron-3-Super, GLM-5, Qwen 3.5)

The release demonstrates extensive hardware support across NVIDIA, AMD, and emerging accelerators.

# NVFP4 GEMM Performance on SM120: Key Metrics

## Tokens/Second Performance

**Baseline (Broken):**
- vLLM native CUTLASS: "Garbage" output, not measurable
- CUTLASS 4.4.1 rebuild: "Garbage" output, not measurable

**Working Solutions:**

| Backend | CUDA Version | Single User | 4-User Concurrent | Architecture |
|---------|--------------|-------------|-------------------|--------------|
| Marlin (W4A16) | 12.8 | 46-49 tok/s | ~37 tok/s/user | Baseline |
| FlashInfer CUTLASS (120a) | 12.8 | 14.6-14.9 tok/s | 6.9-8.5 tok/s/user | compute_120a |
| FlashInfer CUTLASS (120f) | **13.0** | **39.0 tok/s** | **18.2 tok/s/user** | **compute_120f** |

## CUDA Version Speedup: 12.8 → 13.0

Upgrading from CUDA 12.8 to CUDA 13.0 (enabling `compute_120f`) delivered approximately **2.7x throughput improvement** for native FP4 MoE:
- 14.6 tok/s → 39.0 tok/s (single user)
- 6.9 tok/s/user → 18.2 tok/s/user (4-user)

The document states this "nearly triples speed" by enabling "fast TMA WS grouped GEMM tactics that failed with `compute_120a`."

## user_4813494d Cause of Slowdown

FlashInfer's autotuner logs revealed: "All TMA warp-specialized grouped GEMM tactics fail to initialize on SM120 with `compute_120a`," forcing fallback to slower non-TMA implementations. The `compute_120f` flag resolved this initialization failure.
```

# CUDA Version Comparison for SM120 RTX PRO 6000

Based on the provided content, **there is no comparison data between CUDA 12 and CUDA 13** for NVFP4 performance on SM120 RTX PRO 6000.

## What the Content Shows

The document provides **16 tested configurations** but does not differentiate results by CUDA version. The best result reported is:

- **50.5 tok/s sustained decode** using Marlin W4A16 backend with TP=4

The configurations tested include various combinations of:
- MoE backends (Marlin, CUTLASS, FlashInfer)
- Tensor parallelism strategies (TP=2, TP=4, with/without PP or EP)
- MTP settings
- KV cache dtypes

However, **CUDA version is not listed as a tested variable** in the comparison table or methodology section.

## Relevant Context

The author notes that switching from Windows (WSL) to bare metal Linux can improve performance, but CUDA version-specific benchmarking is absent from this analysis. If you need CUDA 12 vs 13 comparisons for this hardware/model combination, that data would need to be obtained separately.

# CUDA Performance Comparison: Blackwell RTX 5090 with llama.cpp

## Key Performance Metrics

**CUDA 12.8 + MMQ (Optimal):**
- Q4_K_M: pp512 = 5,611 t/s | tg128 = 211 t/s
- MXFP4_MOE: pp512 = 6,566 t/s | tg128 = 201 t/s

**CUDA 13.1 + cuBLAS (Degraded):**
- Q4_K_M: pp512 = 772 t/s | tg128 = 121 t/s
- MXFP4_MOE: pp512 = 721 t/s | tg128 = 103 t/s

## Performance Regression

The article documents a **5-6x slowdown** in prompt processing when using CUDA 13.1 instead of 12.8. This occurs because "the Blackwell MMQ kernel crashes with a Segmentation fault" when compiled with CUDA 13.1, forcing fallback to cuBLAS with overhead from quantization decoding.

## Critical Issues

1. **CUDA 13.1 incompatibility**: MMQ kernels are unstable; NVIDIA recommends CUDA 12.8 for Blackwell (SM120)
2. **CMake cache persistence**: The `-DFORCE_CUBLAS=ON` flag persists in `CMakeCache.txt`, silently reducing performance by 5-6x even after reconfiguration
```

- cu13 支持：稳定。sm_120 仍在 nightly 中更成熟，stable 需 `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` 指定；cu128 仍为 2.9.1 默认
- Blackwell 改进：2.10 正式打开 cu130 轨道；sm_120 官方支持 issue 仍在跟踪（#164342, #159207），完整 FP4/WGMMA/TMA 稳定支持依赖 cu13x
- 来源：[pytorch/pytorch#164342](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/164342)、[PyTorch 2.10 RC 公告](https://dev-discuss.pytorch.org/t/pytorch-2-10-final-rc-available/3286)、[cu130 issue #159779](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/159779)

**2. FlashInfer**
- 当前可用版本：**0.6.8.post1**（2026-04-18）。未见 0.7.x / 0.8.x
- cu13 支持：是，commit 显式 "Install nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13] for cu130+"
- Blackwell 关键改进：Port TRT-LLM SM120/SM121 FP4 CUTLASS GEMM（含 PDL）；新增 **MXFP8 GEMM for SM120**、MXFP4/NVFP4 group GEMM (GeForce/Spark)；SM121 tile filter + autotuner 稳健性
- 注意：SM120 NVFP4 mm_fp4 早期 bug（#2577）已随 SM120 patch + CUDA 13.0 `compute_120f` 解决
- 来源：[FlashInfer Releases](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases)、[flashinfer#2577](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2577)、[cutlass#3096](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/issues/3096)

**3. cuDNN**
- 当前：**9.17.0**（SDPA 再优化，benchmark 更新）；9.16.0 为稳定锚点
- Blackwell 改进：9.16 SDPA **bprop 在 CC 10.0 上提升 7%–25%**；9.15 SDPA fprop 引入 flash-attention v4 风格 FP16/BF16 优化（`CUDNN_RESCALE_THRESHOLD=8`、`CUDNN_USE_EX2_EMULATION=1`）；修复 BHSD 之外布局下 SDPA stats 错误
- 来源：[cuDNN 9.16 Release Notes](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/backend/v9.16.0/release-notes.html)、[cudnn-frontend Releases](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/releases)

**4. CUDA Toolkit**
- 当前：**13.2 Update 1**（13.0 → 13.1 → 13.2.x）
- Blackwell sm_120 相关改进：CUDA 12.9 首次引入 sm_12x 支持，CUDA 13.0 扩展 sm_103/sm_110/sm_121；13.1 为 block-scaled **FP4/FP8 + BF16 matmul** 加 perf 路径（CUDA Tile Programming Model）；13.2 Update 1 cuBLASLt 实验性 Grouped GEMM 支持 **NVFP4 输入 + bias epilogue**，Blackwell Grouped GEMM 大 problem size **最高 +20%**
- sm_120 `compute_120f` 通过 CUDA 13.0 启用，修正若干 CUTLASS NVFP4 模板
- 来源：[CUDA 13.2 Release Notes](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-toolkit-release-notes/index.html)、[CUDA 13.1 Blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-cuda-13-1-powers-next-gen-gpu-programming-with-nvidia-cuda-tile-and-performance-gains/)、[CUDA 13.0 Blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/whats-new-and-important-in-cuda-toolkit-13-0/)

I've found comprehensive information about FlashInfer, CUDA 13, SGLang, vLLM, Blackwell, and NVFP4 benchmarks from 2026. Here are the key findings:

## Performance Benchmarks (tokens/s)

At peak throughput (batch size 4096), FlashInfer achieves 1225 TFLOPS, just 3% slower than SGLang (1262 TFLOPS), but at small batches, it's 2.3x slower than SGLang.

vLLM using NVIDIA's NVFP4 quantization hit 8,033 tokens/second, the highest throughput recorded. In comparison, when comparing identical model formats (GPTQ-INT4), SGLang beat vLLM by 17%, reaching 6,395 tokens/second.

For larger deployments, DeepSeek-V3.2 (NVFP4 + TP2) achieves a single-GPU throughput of 7360 TGS (tokens / GPU / second) in a prefill-only scenario, with output throughput of 2816 TGS in a mixed-context scenario (ISL=2k,OSL=1k).

## Key Technical Insights

Three leading MoE backends (vLLM, SGLang, and FlashInfer CuteDSL) were benchmarked running Mixture of Experts models with FP4 quantization on a Blackwell B200 GPU. SGLang achieves 1.32x speedup at batch size 1 (interactive inference) and 2.23x speedup at batch size 128 (decode sweet spot).

FP4 MoE models on Blackwell require explicitly setting VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=1 to enable the FlashInfer FP4 MoE kernel.

- 当前: **Triton 3.3+** 官方 Blackwell 支持（需 CUDA ≥12.8, PyTorch ≥2.7）
- cu13: OK。CUDA 13.0 把 sm_101→sm_110，新增 sm_121 (DGX Spark)，sm_120f 在 12.9 起原生
- Blackwell 收益: NVPTX 后端能生成 sm_120 原生 PTX；cu13 nvcc 新 `--Ofast-compile` 缩短 JIT；但 PTX-lowering 质量对比无公开 benchmark
- URL: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/blackwell-compatibility-guide/index.html

**4. DeepGEMM**
- 最新版: **public-release-260416**（2026-04-16，PR #304）
- cu13: 跟随 PyTorch ≥2.9 要求；Blackwell SM100 一等公民
- Blackwell 收益: Mega MoE 融合 EP dispatch + FP8×FP4 linear + SwiGLU 单 kernel；新 **FP8×FP4 GEMM**、**FP4 Indexer**（MQA logits，利于 MTP/EAGLE）、PDL、JIT CPP 低 CPU 开销
- URL: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/tree/public-release-260416 ， https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/304

**5. nvcc 13 vs 12.8（Triton PTX on sm_120）**
- **无公开实测对比**。已知事实: cu12.8 起 sm_120 cubin 原生；cu12.9 加 `compute_120f`；cu13 新增 `--Ofast-compile`，CCCL 头要求严格预处理。Triton 走 libLLVM NVPTX 自己生成 PTX，ptxas 由 CUDA toolkit 提供 —— 换 cu13 实际只换 ptxas/driver。issue #3096 报告"cu13 + compute_120f"修复 NVFP4 正确性（非 Triton 路径，但佐证 cu13 ptxas 对 sm_120 lowering 更成熟）
- URL: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/pdf/CUDA_Compiler_Driver_NVCC.pdf (Release 13.2, 2026-04-02)

# CUDA 12.8 → CUDA 13 在 Blackwell 上的实测对比（截至 2026-04）

## 正向收益（SM120 / RTX PRO 6000 / 消费 Blackwell）

- (cutlass#3096, NVFP4 MoE grouped GEMM 单路 decode, SM120) CUDA 12.8 compute_120a: 14.6 tok/s → CUDA 13.0 compute_120f: **39.0 tok/s**，~2.7× 加速；4-user 并发 6.9→18.2 tok/s/user。关键：必须用 `compute_120f` 而非 `120a` 才能启用 TMA WS grouped GEMM tactics
- (cutlass#3096, 同场景 vs Marlin W4A16) Marlin 12.8 基线仍是 46–49 tok/s，CUDA 13 + FlashInfer CUTLASS 39 tok/s 仍落后 Marlin
- (NVIDIA CUDA 13.2 release notes, DGX Spark SM121) cuBLASLt NVFP4 / MXFP8 大 M,N GEMM **最高 3×**（SM121，不是消费 SM120）

## 负向 / Regression

- (zenn RTX 5090 llama.cpp benchmark, SM120) CUDA 13.1 使 Blackwell MMQ kernel segfault，fallback 到 cuBLAS：
  - Q4_K_M pp512: 5611 → 772 t/s（−86%）, tg128: 211 → 121 t/s（−43%）
  - MXFP4_MOE pp512: 6566 → 721 t/s（−89%）, tg128: 201 → 103 t/s（−49%）
  - NVIDIA 官方迁移指南明确建议 Blackwell llama.cpp 仍用 **CUDA 12.8**
- (cutlass#3096 / flashinfer#2577 / #2723) SM120 native FP4 MoE 在默认 `compute_120a` 下 CUTLASS grouped GEMM **输出乱码**；需打 FlashInfer patch + 改 `compute_120f`

## 未找到公开数据
- Attention（FlashAttention/FlashInfer prefill decode kernel）在 cu12 vs cu13 的直接 e2e 对比
- SGLang 端到端 LLM throughput 的 cu12/cu13 A/B（HF apsys 博客的 SGLang 1262 TFLOPS 数据用的是 CUDA 13.0，但无 12.x 对照）
- 除 cutlass#3096 外的 NVFP4 TFLOPS cu12 vs cu13 直接对比

## 结论（仅陈述数据，不推断）
消费 SM120 上 cu13 = 机会 + 陷阱：NVFP4 CUTLASS grouped GEMM 有 2.7× 收益但需 `compute_120f`；llama.cpp MMQ 路径在 cu13.1 下崩溃回退 cuBLAS，掉速 5–6×。SGLang 自带 CUTLASS 路径是否会踩同样的 `120a` vs `120f` 坑，需在本机验证。

- [Blackwell llama.cpp CUDA 13 trap benchmark (zenn)](https://zenn.dev/toki_mwc/articles/rtx5090-blackwell-cuda-toolkit-trap-llama-cpp?locale=en)

41	def _profile_can_sync() -> bool:
42	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
43	        return False
44	    try:
45	        return not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
46	    except RuntimeError:
47	        return False

50	def _profile_begin() -> float:
51	    if _profile_can_sync():
52	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
53	    return time.perf_counter()
54	
55	
56	def _profile_end(start: float, bucket: str):
57	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
58	        return
59	    if _profile_can_sync():
60	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
61	    _MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS[bucket] = _MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS.get(bucket, 0.0) + (
62	        time.perf_counter() - start
63	    ) * 1000.0
64	
65	
66	def _profile_step(counter: str, buckets: tuple[str, ...], label: str):
67	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
68	        return
69	    count = _MINICPM_PROFILE_COUNTS.get(counter, 0) + 1
70	    _MINICPM_PROFILE_COUNTS[counter] = count
71	    if count % _MINICPM_PROFILE_INTERVAL != 0:
72	        return
73	    stats = ", ".join(
74	        f"{bucket}={_MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS.get(bucket, 0.0) / count:.3f}ms"
75	        for bucket in buckets
76	    )
77	    print(f"[minicpm-profile] {label} calls={count}, {stats}")

237	        # Query/output data type must stay in compute precision (bf16/fp16);
238	        # only KV cache storage uses the quantized dtype (e.g. fp8_e5m2).
239	        # FlashInfer infers output dtype from q_data_type, and FP8 output
240	        # is not supported in FA2/FA3 backends.

243	        # Create workspace buffers for flashinfer

251	            workspace_size,

261	        self.prefill_wrapper: Optional[BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper] = None
262	
263	        # Track if wrappers have been pre-planned for CUDA graph
264	        self.decode_wrapper_planned = False

368	    def forward(
369	        self,
370	        params: AttentionParams,
371	        layer: RadixAttention,
372	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
373	        """Perform attention computation using flashinfer."""
374	        # Determine if this is prefill or decode based on max_seqlen_q
375	        is_prefill = params.max_seqlen_q > 1
376	        if _MINICPM_PROFILE and is_prefill:
377	            global _FI_FORWARD_PREFILL_DBG
378	            try:
379	                _FI_FORWARD_PREFILL_DBG += 1
380	            except NameError:
381	                _FI_FORWARD_PREFILL_DBG = 1
382	            if _FI_FORWARD_PREFILL_DBG <= 8:
383	                print(f"[minicpm-profile-debug] FI.forward prefill #{_FI_FORWARD_PREFILL_DBG} max_q={params.max_seqlen_q} dec_wrap={params.decode_wrapper is not None}")
384	
385	        # CUDA graph mode: use the pre-configured wrapper from params
386	        if params.decode_wrapper is not None and not is_prefill:
387	            wrapper = params.decode_wrapper
388	            using_preconverted = params.flashinfer_kv_indptr is not None
389	            if not using_preconverted:
390	                # For CUDA graph mode, update wrapper's internal buffers
391	                # Convert sparse_page_table to flashinfer format
392	                bs = params.cache_seqlens.shape[0]
393	                max_sparse_tokens = params.page_table.shape[1]
394	
395	                # Get wrapper's internal buffer shapes to avoid reallocation
396	                kv_indptr_shape = wrapper._paged_kv_indptr_buf.shape
397	                kv_indices_shape = wrapper._paged_kv_indices_buf.shape
398	                kv_last_page_len_shape = wrapper._paged_kv_last_page_len_buf.shape
399	
400	                # Create temporary buffers for conversion (reuse if possible)
401	                if (
402	                    kv_indptr_shape[0] >= bs + 1
403	                    and kv_indices_shape[0] >= bs * max_sparse_tokens
404	                    and kv_last_page_len_shape[0] >= bs
405	                ):
406	                    # Use wrapper's internal buffers directly (no allocation)
407	                    kv_indptr = wrapper._paged_kv_indptr_buf
408	                    kv_indices = wrapper._paged_kv_indices_buf
409	                    kv_last_page_len = wrapper._paged_kv_last_page_len_buf
410	                else:
411	                    # Allocate new buffers if wrapper's buffers are too small
412	                    kv_indptr = torch.zeros(
413	                        bs + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=params.page_table.device
414	                    )
415	                    kv_indices = torch.zeros(
416	                        bs * max_sparse_tokens,
417	                        dtype=torch.int32,
418	                        device=params.page_table.device,
419	                    )
420	                    kv_last_page_len = torch.zeros(
421	                        bs, dtype=torch.int32, device=params.page_table.device
422	                    )
423	
424	                start = _profile_begin()
425	                convert_sparse_page_table_to_flashinfer(
426	                    params.page_table,
427	                    params.cache_seqlens,
428	                    kv_indptr,
429	                    kv_indices,
430	                    kv_last_page_len,
431	                )
432	                _profile_end(start, "graph_decode_convert_ms")
433	        else:
434	            # Non-CUDA graph mode: create wrapper and convert on-the-fly
435	            _conv_start = _profile_begin()
436	            if is_prefill:
437	                wrapper = self._get_or_create_prefill_wrapper()
438	            else:
439	                wrapper = self._get_or_create_decode_wrapper()
440	
441	            # Convert page table format for flashinfer
442	            # Use pre-converted tensors if available (for CUDA graph compatibility),
443	            # otherwise convert on-the-fly (for non-CUDA graph mode)
444	            if (
445	                params.flashinfer_kv_indptr is not None
446	                and params.flashinfer_kv_indices is not None
447	                and params.flashinfer_kv_last_page_len is not None
448	            ):
449	                # Use pre-converted tensors (CUDA graph safe)
450	                kv_indptr = params.flashinfer_kv_indptr
451	                kv_indices = params.flashinfer_kv_indices
452	                kv_last_page_len = params.flashinfer_kv_last_page_len
453	            else:
454	                bs = params.cache_seqlens.shape[0]
455	                max_sparse_tokens = params.page_table.shape[1]
456	
457	                kv_indptr = torch.zeros(
458	                    bs + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=params.page_table.device
459	                )
460	                kv_indices = torch.zeros(
461	                    bs * max_sparse_tokens,
462	                    dtype=torch.int32,
463	                    device=params.page_table.device,
464	                )
465	                kv_last_page_len = torch.zeros(
466	                    bs, dtype=torch.int32, device=params.page_table.device
467	                )
468	
469	                kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_last_page_len = (
470	                    convert_sparse_page_table_to_flashinfer(
471	                        params.page_table,
472	                        params.cache_seqlens,
473	                        kv_indptr,
474	                        kv_indices,
475	                        kv_last_page_len,
476	                    )
477	                )
478	            _profile_end(_conv_start, "fi_convert_ms")
479	
480	            # Call begin_forward to set up the attention plan
481	            # This is required by flashinfer to cache data types and metadata
482	            # Skip only if we're using pre-converted tensors that match the plan
483	            using_preconverted = params.flashinfer_kv_indptr is not None
484	            _begin_start = _profile_begin()
485	            if is_prefill:
486	                if not using_preconverted:
487	                    # Prefill wrapper requires qo_indptr (query indptr)
488	                    qo_indptr = params.cu_seqlens_q
489	                    wrapper.begin_forward(
490	                        qo_indptr,
491	                        kv_indptr,
492	                        kv_indices,
493	                        kv_last_page_len,
494	                        self.num_qo_heads,
495	                        self.num_kv_heads,
496	                        self.head_dim,
497	                        self.page_size,
498	                        q_data_type=self.q_data_type,
499	                        kv_data_type=self.data_type,
500	                        non_blocking=True,
501	                        causal=params.causal,
502	                    )
503	            else:
504	                if not using_preconverted:
505	                    # Decode wrapper uses indptr, indices.
506	                    # Use actual per-sequence head counts from tensors: forward_decode
507	                    # applies a head-group split (tp_q_head_num//2, tp_kv_head_num//2)
508	                    # before calling here, so self.num_qo_heads/num_kv_heads are wrong.
509	                    wrapper.begin_forward(
510	                        kv_indptr,
511	                        kv_indices,
512	                        kv_last_page_len,
513	                        params.q.shape[1],
514	                        params.k_cache.shape[2],
515	                        self.head_dim,
516	                        self.page_size,
517	                        q_data_type=self.q_data_type,
518	                        kv_data_type=self.data_type,
519	                        non_blocking=True,
520	                    )
521	            _profile_end(_begin_start, "fi_begin_forward_ms")
522	
523	        # Perform attention
524	        q_data = params.q
525	        k_data = (params.k_cache, params.v_cache)
526	
527	        if is_prefill:
528	            # Prefill mode: use prefill wrapper
529	            # flashinfer's forward doesn't need cu_seqlens, they are set in begin_forward
530	            if _MINICPM_PROFILE:
531	                global _FA_PREFILL_DEBUG
532	                try:
533	                    _FA_PREFILL_DEBUG += 1
534	                except NameError:
535	                    _FA_PREFILL_DEBUG = 1
536	                if _FA_PREFILL_DEBUG <= 5:
537	                    print(f"[minicpm-profile-debug] FA prefill call #{_FA_PREFILL_DEBUG} max_q={params.max_seqlen_q}")
538	            _fa_start = _profile_begin()
539	            o = wrapper.forward(
540	                q_data,
541	                k_data,
542	                causal=params.causal,
543	                sm_scale=params.softmax_scale,
544	                window_left=(
545	                    params.window_size[0] if params.window_size[0] != -1 else -1
546	                ),
547	                logits_soft_cap=params.softcap if params.softcap > 0 else None,
548	            )
549	            _profile_end(_fa_start, "stage2_fa_prefill_ms")
550	        else:
551	            # Decode mode: use decode wrapper (also sparse prefill fallback)
552	            _dec_start = _profile_begin()
553	            o = wrapper.forward(
554	                q_data,
555	                k_data,
556	                sm_scale=params.softmax_scale,
557	                logits_soft_cap=params.softcap if params.softcap > 0 else None,
558	            )
559	            _profile_end(_dec_start, "fi_decode_fwd_ms")
560	            _profile_end(_dec_start, "graph_decode_forward_ms")
561	            if params.decode_wrapper is not None:
562	                _profile_step(
563	                    "graph_decode_calls",
564	                    ("graph_decode_convert_ms", "graph_decode_forward_ms"),
565	                    "flashinfer-graph-decode",
566	                )
567	
568	        return o

583	def create_attention_kernel(

585	    model_runner,
586	) -> AttentionKernel:
587	    """Factory function to create the appropriate attention kernel.
588	
589	    Args:
590	        kernel_type: Type of kernel to create ('flash_attn' or 'flashinfer')
591	        model_runner: The model runner instance
592	
593	    Returns:
594	        An instance of the requested attention kernel
595	
596	    Raises:
597	        ValueError: If kernel_type is not recognized
598	    """
599	    if kernel_type == "flash_attn":
600	        return FlashAttentionKernel()
601	    elif kernel_type == "flashinfer":
602	        return FlashInferKernel(model_runner)
603	    else:
604	        raise ValueError(f"Unknown attention kernel type: {kernel_type}")

43	def batched_gather(a, cu_seqlen_q, select):
44	    #
45	    select_bs = len(select)
46	    select = torch.tensor(select, device="cpu")
47	    starts = cu_seqlen_q[select]
48	    ends = cu_seqlen_q[select + 1]
49	    lengths = ends - starts
50	
51	    max_len = lengths.max()
52	    local_offsets = torch.arange(max_len, device=a.device)[None, :]
53	    mask = local_offsets < lengths[:, None]
54	
55	    local_offsets = local_offsets.expand(select_bs, -1)[mask]
56	
57	    starts_expanded = starts.repeat_interleave(lengths)
58	    index = starts_expanded + local_offsets
59	
60	    return a[index]

63	def compress_k_core_new(
64	    full_compressed_k,  # output
65	    layer,
66	    batch,
67	    k_stride,
68	    key_cache,
69	    token_table,
70	    compressed_k_table,
71	    new_k_token_nums,
72	    cu_new_k_token_nums,
73	    history_compress_k_token_nums,
74	    cu_new_compress_k_token_nums,
75	    new_compress_k_token_nums,
76	    total_compress_k_token_nums,
77	    cu_total_compress_k_token_nums,
78	    kernel_size,
79	    kernel_stride,
80	    max_context_length,
81	):
82	
83	    head_num_k = key_cache.shape[1]
84	    head_dim = key_cache.shape[2]
85	
86	    # ==============================================================================
87	    # BUFFER ALLOCATION
88	    # ==============================================================================
89	
90	    # Use provided explicit parameters for buffer allocation
91	    # max_chunks_per_seq is already the maximum possible chunks for any sequence
92	    # given max_context_length, kernel_size, and kernel_stride
93	    max_chunks_per_seq = max(0, (max_context_length - kernel_size) // kernel_stride + 1)
94	
95	    # ==============================================================================
96	    # Launch kernel for ALL chunks (history + new)
97	    # ==============================================================================
98	    # Grid: (batch, max_chunks_per_seq, head_num_k)
99	    # - chunk_in_seq in [0, history_compress): process HISTORY chunks
100	    # - chunk_in_seq in [history_compress, total_chunks_in_seq): process NEW chunks
101	    #
102	    # max_chunks_per_seq is already the maximum possible chunks for any sequence,
103	    # so it's sufficient for both history and new chunks.
104	    #
105	    # All operations are in a single kernel, CUDA graph compatible.
106	
107	    # Limit grid size to avoid too many thread blocks
108	    # If max_chunks_per_seq > max_grid_chunks, kernel will loop to handle remaining chunks
109	    MAX_GRID_CHUNKS = 1024  # Adjustable limit for grid dimension
110	    max_grid_chunks = min(max_chunks_per_seq, MAX_GRID_CHUNKS)
111	
112	    BLOCK_SIZE = triton.next_power_of_2(head_dim)
113	    # Grid size is now limited, kernel uses loop to handle all chunks
114	    grid = (batch, max_grid_chunks, head_num_k)
115	
116	    compress_k_complete_kernel_new[grid](
117	        key_cache,
118	        token_table,
119	        cu_new_k_token_nums,
120	        history_compress_k_token_nums,
121	        k_stride,
122	        compressed_k_table,
123	        cu_new_compress_k_token_nums,
124	        cu_total_compress_k_token_nums,
125	        total_compress_k_token_nums,
126	        full_compressed_k,
127	        batch,
128	        max_chunks_per_seq,
129	        token_table.shape[1],
130	        compressed_k_table.shape[1],
131	        head_num_k,
132	        head_dim,
133	        kernel_size,
134	        kernel_stride,
135	        BLOCK_SIZE,
136	        max_grid_chunks,  # Pass the limit to kernel for loop control
137	    )
138	
139	    return

164	    # token_table [batch_size, token_num]: the pre-allocated locs of normal tokens
165	    # k1_table [batch_size, total_compress_k1_token_num]: the pre-allocated locs of compress k1 tokens
166	    # k2_table [batch_size, total_compress_k2_token_num]: the pre-allocated locs of compress k2 tokens
167	    # theses arguments should be dirrectly passed in
168	
169	    # get key cache ptr, zero over head
170	    key_cache = forward_batch.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id)
171	    key_cache = key_cache.view(-1, layer.tp_k_head_num, layer.head_dim)
172	
173	    ##################### prepare of computation ######################
174	
175	    # deal with k1
176	    compress_k_core_new(
177	        full_compressed_k1,
178	        layer,
179	        batch,
180	        k1_stride,
181	        key_cache,
182	        metadata.page_table,
183	        metadata.k1.table,
184	        metadata.k1.new_token_nums,
185	        metadata.k1.cu_new_token_nums,
186	        metadata.k1.history_compress_token_nums,
187	        metadata.k1.cu_new_compress_token_nums,
188	        metadata.k1.new_compress_token_nums,
189	        metadata.k1.total_compress_token_nums,
190	        metadata.k1.cu_total_compress_token_nums,
191	        k1_l,
192	        k1_stride,
193	        max_context_length,
194	    )
195	
196	    # deal with k2
197	    compress_k_core_new(
198	        full_compressed_k2,
199	        layer,
200	        batch,
201	        k2_stride,
202	        key_cache,
203	        metadata.page_table,

206	        metadata.k2.cu_new_token_nums,
207	        metadata.k2.history_compress_token_nums,
208	        metadata.k2.cu_new_compress_token_nums,
209	        metadata.k2.new_compress_token_nums,

211	        metadata.k2.cu_total_compress_token_nums,
212	        k2_l,
213	        k2_stride,
214	        max_context_length,
215	    )
216	
217	    return

220	def compress_k_core_new_padded(
221	    full_compressed_k,  # output
222	    layer,
223	    batch,
224	    k_stride,
225	    key_cache,
226	    token_table,
227	    compressed_k_table,
228	    new_k_token_nums,
229	    cu_new_k_token_nums,
230	    history_compress_k_token_nums,
231	    cu_new_compress_k_token_nums,
232	    new_compress_k_token_nums,
233	    total_compress_k_token_nums,
234	    cu_total_compress_k_token_nums,
235	    kernel_size,
236	    kernel_stride,
237	    max_context_length,
238	):
239	    """Padded layout version: stores data in batch-major order for reshape compatibility."""
240	    head_num_k = key_cache.shape[1]
241	    head_dim = key_cache.shape[2]
242	
243	    # Compute max_chunks_per_seq for padded layout
244	    # Must match: batch_size * max_context_length // kernel_stride
245	    max_chunks_per_seq = max_context_length // kernel_stride
246	
247	    MAX_GRID_CHUNKS = 1024  # Adjustable limit for grid dimension
248	    max_grid_chunks = min(max_chunks_per_seq, MAX_GRID_CHUNKS)
249	
250	    BLOCK_SIZE = triton.next_power_of_2(head_dim)
251	    grid = (batch, max_grid_chunks, head_num_k)
252	
253	    compress_k_complete_kernel_new_padded[grid](
254	        key_cache,
255	        token_table,
256	        cu_new_k_token_nums,
257	        history_compress_k_token_nums,
258	        k_stride,
259	        compressed_k_table,
260	        cu_new_compress_k_token_nums,
261	        cu_total_compress_k_token_nums,
262	        total_compress_k_token_nums,
263	        full_compressed_k,
264	        batch,
265	        max_chunks_per_seq,
266	        token_table.shape[1],
267	        compressed_k_table.shape[1],
268	        head_num_k,
269	        head_dim,
270	        kernel_size,
271	        kernel_stride,
272	        BLOCK_SIZE,
273	        max_grid_chunks,
274	    )
275	    return

342	def allocate_and_compress_keys(
343	    layer,
344	    forward_batch,
345	    metadata: "FlashAttentionMetadata",
346	    k1_token_nums: int,
347	    k2_token_nums: int,
348	    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
349	    device: torch.device = None,
350	    max_context_length: int = 32768,
351	    split_stage1: bool = False,
352	):
353	    """Allocate compressed key tensors and run compression.
354	
355	    Args:
356	        layer: Model layer with head configuration
357	        forward_batch: Forward batch info
358	        metadata: FlashAttention metadata
359	        k1_token_nums: Number of k1 tokens to allocate
360	        k2_token_nums: Number of k2 tokens to allocate
361	        dtype: Tensor data type (default: bfloat16)
362	        device: Tensor device (default: layer device)
363	        max_context_length: Maximum context length for the model (default: 32768)
364	        split_stage1: If True, use padded kernel
365	
366	    Returns:
367	        Tuple of (full_compressed_k1, full_compressed_k2)
368	    """
369	    if device is None:
370	        device = (
371	            layer.device if hasattr(layer, "device") else torch.cuda.current_device()
372	        )
373	
374	    full_compressed_k1 = torch.full(
375	        (k1_token_nums, layer.tp_k_head_num, layer.head_dim), dtype=dtype, device=device, fill_value=float('-inf')
376	    )
377	    full_compressed_k2 = torch.full(
378	        (k2_token_nums, layer.tp_k_head_num, layer.head_dim), dtype=dtype, device=device, fill_value=float('-inf')
379	    )
380	
381	    if split_stage1:
382	        get_compress_k_v2_padded(
383	            layer,
384	            forward_batch,
385	            metadata,
386	            full_compressed_k1,
387	            full_compressed_k2,
388	            max_context_length=max_context_length,
389	        )
390	    else:
391	        get_compress_k_v2(
392	            layer,
393	            forward_batch,
394	            metadata,
395	            full_compressed_k1,
396	            full_compressed_k2,
397	            max_context_length=max_context_length,
398	        )
399	
400	    return full_compressed_k1, full_compressed_k2
401

403	def compressed_attention(
404	    q: torch.Tensor,
405	    k: torch.Tensor,
406	    k2: torch.Tensor,
407	    kernel_size: int,
408	    kernel_stride: int,
409	    block_size: int,
410	    topk: int,
411	    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor,
412	    cu_seqlens_k: torch.Tensor,
413	    cu_seqlens_k2: torch.Tensor,
414	    max_seqlen_q: int,
415	    # max_seqlen_k: int,
416	    max_context_len: int,
417	    sm_scale: Optional[float] = None,
418	    init_blocks: int = 1,
419	    local_blocks: int = 2,
420	    cache_lens: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
421	    total_q: int = -1,
422	    cu_seqlens_q_adjusted: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
423	    max_seqlen_q_adjusted: Optional[int] = None,
424	    split_stage1: bool = False,
425	) -> torch.Tensor:
426	    """Compressed attention computation for sparse attention.
427	
428	    Computes attention scores between query and compressed keys (k and k2),
429	    then performs max pooling and selects top-k blocks.
430	
431	    Args:
432	        q: Query tensor, shape (total_q_len, num_heads, head_dim)
433	        k: Compressed key tensor k1, shape (total_k_len, num_heads, head_dim)
434	        k2: Compressed key tensor k2, shape (total_k_len, num_heads, head_dim)
435	        kernel_size: Size of compression kernel
436	        kernel_stride: Stride of compression kernel
437	        block_size: Size of attention blocks
438	        topk: Number of top blocks to select
439	        cu_seqlens_q: Cumulative sequence lengths for query, shape (batch_size + 1)
440	        cu_seqlens_k: Cumulative sequence lengths for k, shape (batch_size + 1)
441	        cu_seqlens_k2: Cumulative sequence lengths for k2, shape (batch_size + 1)
442	        max_seqlen_q: Maximum sequence length in query
443	        max_seqlen_k: Maximum sequence length in key
444	        sm_scale: Softmax scaling factor (unused, kept for compatibility)
445	        init_blocks: Number of initial blocks to always attend to
446	        local_blocks: Number of local blocks to consider
447	        cache_lens: Cache lengths for each batch (optional)
448	        total_q: Total number of queries (used for pooling)
449	        cu_seqlens_q_adjusted: Adjusted cumulative sequence lengths for query (for stage1 optimization)
450	        max_seqlen_q_adjusted: Adjusted maximum sequence length for query (for stage1 optimization)
451	
452	    Returns:
453	        Top-k block indices, shape (num_heads, total_q_len, topk)
454	    """
455	    with torch.no_grad():
456	        batch_size = cu_seqlens_q.shape[0] - 1
457	
458	        current_ratio = q.shape[-2] // k.shape[-2]
459	        required_ratio = 16
460	        if current_ratio < required_ratio:
461	            repeat_times = required_ratio // current_ratio
462	            q = q.repeat_interleave(repeat_times, dim=-2)
463	
464	        is_prefilling = max_seqlen_q > 1
465	
466	        # Stage1 optimization: q_idx computation is no longer needed
467	        if is_prefilling:
468	            if cache_lens is None:
469	                cache_lens = torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device)
470	        #     q_idx = torch.cat(
471	        #         [
472	        #             (
473	        #                 torch.arange(
474	        #                     cu_seqlens_q[i + 1] - cu_seqlens_q[i], device=q.device
475	        #                 )
476	        #                 + cache_lens[i]
477	        #             )
478	        #             // block_size
479	        #             for i in range(batch_size)
480	        #         ],
481	        #         dim=0,
482	        #     )
483	        # else:
484	        #     q_idx = cache_lens // block_size
485	
486	
487	        # split-stage1 -> bmm+softmax+reduce_sum
488	        if not is_prefilling and split_stage1:
489	            batch_size = q.shape[0]
490	            k1_len = k.shape[0]
491	            q_head = q.shape[1]
492	            kv_head = k.shape[1]
493	            group_size = q_head // kv_head
494	            head_dim = k.shape[2]
495	            q_reshape = (
496	                q.reshape(batch_size, 1, q_head, head_dim)
497	                    .transpose(1, 2)
498	                    .reshape(batch_size, kv_head, group_size, head_dim)
499	                    .transpose(0, 1)
500	                    .reshape(-1, group_size, head_dim)
501	            )
502	            k_reshape = (
503	                k.reshape(batch_size, k1_len // batch_size, kv_head, head_dim)
504	                .transpose(1, 2)
505	                .transpose(-2, -1)
506	                .transpose(0, 1)
507	                .reshape(-1, head_dim, k1_len // batch_size)
508	            )
509	    
510	            scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(head_dim)
511	            score = torch.bmm(q_reshape, k_reshape).mul_(scale)
512	            torch.nan_to_num(score, nan=float("-inf"), posinf=float("-inf"), out=score)
513	            torch.softmax(score, dim=-1, out=score)
514	            score = score.reshape(kv_head, batch_size, group_size, k1_len // batch_size).sum(dim=2)
515	        else:
516	            _stage1_start = _profile_begin()
517	            score = infllmv2_attn_stage1(
518	                q.contiguous(),
519	                k.contiguous(),
520	                k2.contiguous(),
521	                cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens_q_adjusted,
522	                cu_seqlens_k=cu_seqlens_k,
523	                cu_seqlens_v=cu_seqlens_k2,
524	                max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen_q_adjusted,
525	                max_seqlen_k=max_context_len // kernel_stride,
526	                causal=is_prefilling
527	            )
528	            _profile_end(
529	                _stage1_start,
530	                "stage1_score_prefill_ms" if is_prefilling else "stage1_score_decode_ms",
531	            )
532	
533	        _pool_start = _profile_begin()
534	        block_score = max_pooling_1d_varlen(
535	            score.contiguous(),
536	            cu_seqlens_q,
537	            cu_seqlens_k,
538	            cache_lens,
539	            max_seqlen_q,
540	            # max_seqlen_k,
541	            max_context_len,
542	            local_blocks=local_blocks,
543	            init_blocks=init_blocks,
544	            block_size=block_size,
545	            stride=kernel_stride,
546	            total_q=total_q,
547	        )
548	        _profile_end(
549	            _pool_start,
550	            "max_pool_prefill_ms" if is_prefilling else "max_pool_decode_ms",
551	        )
552	
553	        _topk_start = _profile_begin()
554	        topk_idx = block_score.topk(topk, dim=-1).indices.sort(-1).values
555	        # Stage1 optimization: skip q_idx filtering
556	        # topk_idx[topk_idx > q_idx[None, :, None]] = -1
557	        topk_idx = topk_idx.to(torch.int32)
558	        _profile_end(
559	            _topk_start,
560	            "topk_select_prefill_ms" if is_prefilling else "topk_select_decode_ms",
561	        )
562	
563	    return topk_idx
564	
565	
566	def compressed_attention_tilelang(
567	    q: torch.Tensor,
568	    k: torch.Tensor,
569	    k2: torch.Tensor,
570	    kernel_size: int,
571	    kernel_stride: int,
572	    block_size: int,
573	    topk: int,
574	    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor,
575	    cu_seqlens_k: torch.Tensor,
576	    cu_seqlens_k2: torch.Tensor,
577	    max_seqlen_q: int,
578	    max_seqlen_k: int,
579	    sm_scale: float = None,
580	    init_blocks: int = 1,
581	    local_blocks: int = 2,
582	    cache_lens=None,
583	    fused_kernel=None,
584	    max_cache_len=-1,
585	) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
586	    """
587	    使用 tilelang online topk kernel 计算 compressed attention topk indices
588	    """
589	    with torch.no_grad():
590	        batch_size = cu_seqlens_q.shape[0] - 1
591	
592	        # Check if it's prefilling stage
593	        # Use max_seqlen_q > 1 to avoid .item() call for CUDA Graph compatibility
594	        is_prefilling = cache_lens is None or max_seqlen_q > 1
595	
596	        # Fixed max_cache_len for CUDA Graph compatibility (avoid .item() calls)
597	        # max_cache_len = 525312  # 512k
598	
599	
600	        # Get tensor dimensions
601	        # q shape: [total_q_len, num_kv_heads, groups, head_dim] or [total_q_len, num_heads, head_dim]
602	        # k shape: [total_k_len, num_kv_heads, head_dim]
603	        total_q_len = q.shape[0]
604	        total_k_len = k.shape[0]
605	        num_kv_heads = k.shape[1]
606	        head_dim = k.shape[2]
607	
608	        # Determine num_heads and groups
609	        # if q.dim() == 4:
610	        #     groups = q.shape[2]
611	        #     num_heads = num_kv_heads * groups
612	        #     # Reshape q from [total_q_len, num_kv_heads, groups, head_dim] to [total_q_len * groups, num_kv_heads, head_dim]
613	        #     q_kernel = q.transpose(1, 2).reshape(total_q_len * groups, num_kv_heads, head_dim).contiguous()
614	        # else:
615	        num_heads = q.shape[1]
616	        groups = num_heads // num_kv_heads
617	        # q shape: [total_q_len, num_heads, head_dim]
618	        # Need to reshape to [total_q_len * groups, num_kv_heads, head_dim]
619	        q_kernel = q.view(total_q_len, num_kv_heads, groups, head_dim)
620	        q_kernel = q_kernel.transpose(1, 2).reshape(total_q_len * groups, num_kv_heads, head_dim).contiguous()
621	
622	        k_kernel = k.contiguous()
623	
624	        # Compute pooled_k_len using infllmv2 formula (based on block count):
625	        # total_len = max_seqlen_q + cache_len
626	        # out_len = (total_len + block_size - 1) // block_size
627	        if is_prefilling:
628	            # Prefill: use the actual max_seqlen_q
629	            total_len = max_seqlen_q
630	            pooled_k_len = (max_cache_len + block_size - 1) // block_size
631	        else:
632	            # Decode: use fixed max_cache_len for CUDA Graph compatibility
633	            # Kernel uses actual_pooled_k_len internally for dynamic bounds checking
634	            pooled_k_len = (max_cache_len + block_size - 1) // block_size
635	            # assert decode_fused_kernel is not None, "decode_fused_kernel is not initialized"
636	
637	        assert fused_kernel is not None, "fused_kernel is not initialized"
638	
639	
640	        # Pooling parameters - aligned with infllmv2_cuda_impl:
641	        # block_stride = block_size // kernel_stride = 64 // 16 = 4
642	        # pad_len = kernel_size // kernel_stride - 1 = 32 // 16 - 1 = 1
643	        # num_offs = kernel_size // kernel_stride + block_size // kernel_stride - 1 = 2 + 4 - 1 = 5
644	        pooling_block_stride = block_size // kernel_stride  # = 64 // 16 = 4
645	        pooling_pad_len = kernel_size // kernel_stride - 1  # = 32 // 16 - 1 = 1
646	        pooling_num_offs = kernel_size // kernel_stride + block_size // kernel_stride - 1  # = 2 + 4 - 1 = 5
647	
648	        # Compute actual output topk (same as original: min(topk, num_blocks))
649	        output_topk = min(topk, pooled_k_len)
650	
651	        # For the kernel, we need power of 2 topk
652	        topk_power2 = tilelang.math.next_power_of_2(output_topk)
653	        kernel_topk = min(topk_power2, pooled_k_len)
654	        # Make sure it's still power of 2
655	        if kernel_topk != tilelang.math.next_power_of_2(kernel_topk):
656	            kernel_topk = tilelang.math.next_power_of_2(kernel_topk) // 2
657	        kernel_topk = max(8, kernel_topk)  # Minimum topk for kernel
658	
659	        # Determine dtype string
660	        if q.dtype == torch.float16:
661	            dtype_str = "float16"
662	        elif q.dtype == torch.bfloat16:
663	            dtype_str = "bfloat16"
664	        else:
665	            dtype_str = "bfloat16"
666	
667	        # Allocate output tensors
668	        topk_indices = torch.full((num_kv_heads, total_q_len, kernel_topk), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device)
669	        topk_values = torch.full((num_kv_heads, total_q_len, kernel_topk), float('-inf'), dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
670	
671	        if is_prefilling:
672	            # =================================================================
673	            # PREFILL: Use bucketed max_seqlen_q and pooled_k_len
674	            # Compiles once per unique bucket combination
675	            # Supports chunk prefill with cache_lens tensor
676	            # =================================================================
677	            # bucketed_max_seqlen_q = _bucket_size(max_seqlen_q)
678	            bucketed_pooled_k_len = _bucket_size(pooled_k_len)
679	            # Also bucket actual_max_seqlen_q/k to reduce kernel recompilation
680	            # bucketed_actual_max_seqlen_q = _bucket_size(max_seqlen_q)
681	            # bucketed_actual_max_seqlen_k = _bucket_size(max_seqlen_k)
682	
683	            # Prepare cache_lens tensor for chunk prefill support
684	            # For standard prefill: cache_lens is None -> use zeros
685	            # For chunk prefill: cache_lens has values -> use as-is
686	            if cache_lens is None:
687	                cache_lens_tensor = torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device)
688	            else:
689	                cache_lens_tensor = cache_lens.to(torch.int32)
690	
691	
692	
693	            # Run prefill kernel with cache_lens for chunk prefill support
694	            fused_kernel(q_kernel, k_kernel, cu_seqlens_q, cu_seqlens_k, cache_lens_tensor, topk_indices, topk_values)
695	        else:
696	            # =================================================================
697	            # DECODE: max_seqlen_q=1 (fixed), cache_lens passed as tensor
698	            # Compiles ONCE and reuses for all decode steps!
699	            # =================================================================
700	            bucketed_pooled_k_len = _bucket_size(pooled_k_len)
701	
702	            # Prepare cache_lens as tensor (runtime value, not compile-time constant!)
703	            cache_lens_tensor = cache_lens.to(torch.int32)
704	
705	            # kernel = fused_attn_pooling_online_topk_decode(
706	            #     batch_size=batch_size,
707	            #     groups=groups,
708	            #     heads=num_heads,
709	            #     dim=head_dim,
710	            #     topk=kernel_topk,
711	            #     pooled_k_len=bucketed_pooled_k_len,
712	            #     m_block_dim=16,
713	            #     block_stride=pooling_block_stride,
714	            #     pad_len=pooling_pad_len,
715	            #     num_offs=pooling_num_offs,
716	            #     block_size=block_size,
717	            #     init_blocks=init_blocks,
718	            #     local_blocks=local_blocks,
719	            #     dtype_str=dtype_str
720	            # )
721	
722	            # Run decode kernel with cache_lens as tensor
723	            fused_kernel(q_kernel, k_kernel, cu_seqlens_q, cu_seqlens_k, cache_lens_tensor, topk_indices, topk_values)
724	
725	        # Note: q_idx masking is handled inside the kernel via causal_mask
726	        # which sets scores to -1e9 for K blocks beyond the causal boundary.
727	        # These blocks won't be selected in topk due to their low scores.
728	
729	        # Sort with -1 values at the end (match original behavior)
730	        # Replace -1 with large value, sort, then replace back
731	        large_val = pooled_k_len + 1000  # Any value larger than max valid index
732	        topk_for_sort = topk_indices.clone()
733	        topk_for_sort[topk_for_sort == -1] = large_val
734	        topk_idx = topk_for_sort.sort(-1).values
735	        topk_idx[topk_idx == large_val] = -1
736	
737	        # Truncate to output_topk (same as original: min(topk, num_blocks))
738	        topk_idx = topk_idx[:, :, :output_topk]
739	
740	        return topk_idx
741

811	@dataclass
812	class SparseConfig:
813	    """Configuration for sparse attention in MiniCPM models.
814	
815	    This dataclass stores all sparse attention configuration parameters,
816	    including kernel sizes, block sizes, top-K selection, and model
817	    architecture parameters.
818	
819	    The configuration is derived from the model's hf_config and
820	    model_config, and is used by SparseBatchAnalyzer to compute
821	    metadata for sparse attention batches.
822	    """
823	
824	    # Basic sparse config parameters (from hf_config)
825	    sparse_len: int  # Threshold for activating sparse attention
826	    sparse_topk: int  # Number of top-K global blocks to select
827	    kernel_size: int  # Kernel size for compressed key computation
828	    kernel_stride: int  # Kernel stride for compressed key computation
829	    block_size: int  # Block size for top-K selection
830	    window_size: int  # Window size for sliding window attention
831	    dense_len: int  # Length of dense attention at beginning
832	
833	    # Model architecture parameters
834	    head_dim: int  # Dimension of each attention head
835	    num_kv_heads: int  # Number of key-value heads
836	    head_group_num: int  # Number of head groups for sparse attention
837	
838	    # Compressor kernel sizes
839	    k1_kernel_size: int
840	    k1_kernel_stride: int
841	    k2_kernel_size: int
842	    k2_kernel_stride: int
843	
844	    @property
845	    def local_blocks(self) -> int:
846	        """Number of local blocks (window_size // block_size)."""
847	        return self.window_size // self.block_size
848	
849	    @property
850	    def sparse_topk_total(self) -> int:
851	        """Total top-K including local blocks (topk + local_blocks)."""
852	        return self.sparse_topk + self.local_blocks
853	
854	    @property
855	    def num_sparse_topk_tokens(self) -> int:
856	        """Total number of tokens in sparse top-K selection."""
857	        return self.block_size * self.sparse_topk_total
858	
859	    @classmethod
860	    def from_model_config(cls, hf_config, model_config) -> "SparseConfig":
861	        """Create SparseConfig from model configuration.
862	
863	        Args:
864	            hf_config: The HuggingFace model config (MiniCPMHybridConfig)
865	            model_config: The SGLang model config
866	
867	        Returns:
868	            SparseConfig instance with all parameters set
869	        """
870	        sparse_topk = hf_config.sparse_topk
871	        kernel_size = hf_config.sparse_kernel_size
872	        kernel_stride = hf_config.sparse_kernel_stride
873	        block_size = hf_config.sparse_block_size
874	        window_size = hf_config.sparse_window_size
875	        dense_len = hf_config.sparse_dense_len
876	
877	        head_dim = model_config.head_dim
878	        num_kv_heads = model_config.num_key_value_heads
879	        head_group_num = model_config.num_key_value_heads
880	
881	        k1_kernel_size = kernel_size
882	        k1_kernel_stride = kernel_stride
883	        k2_kernel_size = kernel_size * 4
884	        k2_kernel_stride = kernel_stride * 4
885	
886	        return cls(
887	            sparse_len=dense_len,
888	            sparse_topk=sparse_topk,
889	            kernel_size=kernel_size,
890	            kernel_stride=kernel_stride,
891	            block_size=block_size,
892	            window_size=window_size,
893	            dense_len=dense_len,
894	            head_dim=head_dim,
895	            num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
896	            head_group_num=head_group_num,
897	            k1_kernel_size=k1_kernel_size,
898	            k1_kernel_stride=k1_kernel_stride,
899	            k2_kernel_size=k2_kernel_size,
900	            k2_kernel_stride=k2_kernel_stride,
901	        )
